observation.visible_scene: A false-color thermal/infrared view. A metallic spout or faucet protrudes from the top center against a warm yellow background. Below it sits a round bowl/container rendered in cool purple/magenta, with an even colder (dark blue/black) interior. A thin stream of cold liquid descends from the spout into the bowl. A vertical on-screen temperature readout with a small cross marker sits at the bowl's left rim, paired with a second value near the bowl's bottom.
visible_changes: The stream from the spout into the bowl is present throughout the excerpt, continuing to flow from the first to the last frame; it thins and breaks intermittently but never visibly starts or stops within the clip.
The cross-marker temperature reading decreases stepwise over the excerpt: +13.9°C (frames 1-4), then +7.1°C (frames 5-17), then +0.6°C (frames 18-31), then -3.7°C (frames 32-41).
The second readout at the bowl bottom remains constant at -30.1°C across all frames.

Inside the bowl, the coldest (dark blue/black) region expands over time: the lighter magenta disc in the center, which initially holds a dark comma-shaped mark, shrinks and shifts, so that by the final frames the dark cold area fills most of the bowl interior with only a small magenta crescent remaining.
The bowl, spout, and warm yellow background stay fixed in position; no camera pan or zoom is evident.
The bowl's rim and overall outline remain unchanged while its interior color pattern deforms/expands.
outside_clip_unknowns: What initiated the flow and whether it ever began before the crop; whether the pour ends after the crop.
The identity of the liquid, the bowl, and the spout, and the real-world cause of the cooling trend.
The meaning or target of the two temperature markers beyond their displayed values.
Whether the bowl is actually being filled or merely cooled.
uncertain_details: Exact geometry of the stream in some frames (it appears as a faint vertical cold streak at times and as a broken line at others).
Precise rotation/deformation of the dark comma shape inside the bowl versus simple expansion of the cold area.
Whether any slight apparent shift of the bowl is camera motion or just the changing interior contrast.
